From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Leah Kim <leah.kim@cardinalht.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PoC planning: Cardinal HealthTech — deployment mode & PoC plan

Hi Samir / Leah,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the clarity on your regulatory and throughput constraints. Quick recap plus a proposed PoC plan so we can lock the deployment mode and next steps.

Recap of requirements you emphasized:
- PHI/data residency: must keep PHI within our US VPC and meet your legal team's controls.
- Latency: p95 inference latency target ~<150ms for the clinician-facing summaries.
- Throughput: burst to ~30 concurrent sessions during peak hours, sustained ~8–12 qps.
- Auditability: token-level audit logs and retention for 12 months (SOC2/hipaa-aligned).

Deployment modes considered (pros/cons we discussed):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, lower operational overhead, but needs contractual data handling guarantees — likely requires VPC peering or a Private lane for PHI (we can discuss DPA addendum).
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool (good for predictable throughput and lower unit cost) but still requires network isolation options and approval for PHI flows.
- Private VPC / On-prem: strongest control for PHI and compliance — longer setup + procurement but likely the cleanest from a security signoff perspective.

Proposed 6-week PoC (goal: choose final deployment mode and validate SLOs):
Week 1: Kickoff & access — exchange credentials, security questionnaire (see attached), confirm success criteria and stakeholder roster.
Week 2–3: Integration & baseline runs — integration against a shadow endpoint, run 1k representative clinical prompts, collect latency/throughput traces.
Week 4: Performance tuning — enable batching/caching, test Dedicated vs Private routing (if available), measure cost delta.
Week 5: Security validation — run audit/log export, review KMS integration and retention.
Week 6: Decision review & next steps — present results, recommended deployment mode, and contract path.

Success criteria (proposed, please adjust):
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms for the canonical prompt set.
- Quality: community-vetted prompt evals show no regression vs baseline (sample pass rate >= 90%).
- Scalability: sustain 12 qps with less than 5% error rate and graceful degradation beyond 30 concurrent sessions.
- Compliance: audit logs exported and accessible; KMS integration validated.
- Cost: unit cost estimate within the budget threshold you provide (we can model three scenarios).

Next actions I'd suggest now:
1) You confirm security owner + procurement contact (I think that is Procurement and Leah is product owner?).
2) We set a 45–60 minute technical deep-dive with your infra/security team this week to validate the Private VPC constraints.
3) I’ll send the PoC scope and a draft timeline (attached).

Attachments included: Cardinal_PoC_Scope.pdf (PoC scope + data flow), security-questions-cardinal.xlsx (short questionnaire).

If the plan looks good I can spin up the internal PoC request and link Ben (account lead) and Lauren (CS lead) for cost & ops planning.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side.

1) Security first: given the PHI scope we are strongly leaning toward Private VPC. Our security team requires:
   - Dedicated customer-controlled KMS (no shared keys),
   - VPC peering or direct connect option (no public internet),
   - Audit logs pushed to our S3 with the ability to set lifecycle policies.

2) Timeline: procurement has a hard freeze window from 4/20–5/05, so we’d like to complete the PoC kickoff and the tech deep-dive before 4/20 if possible. Is that realistic?

3) Budget: high level — if Private VPC is required we will need a ballpark for committed monthly cost so we can pre-clear with finance. If you can provide 3 scenarios (Hosted w/ controls, Dedicated reserved, Private VPC estimate) that will help.

Also looping procurement (procurement@cardinalht.com) on the thread. Leah will be our internal PM and will coordinate schedule.

On the success criteria: the latency target of p95<150ms is non-negotiable for launch. Quality threshold is fine as-is.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Samir
CTO, Cardinal HealthTech
